meta.title: The Note That Fights the Chord
meta.summary: An avoid note is a scale tone a half step above a chord tone — Ionian has exactly one over A, Mixolydian keeps it, and Lydian's raised fourth is the only one of this chapter's three modes without it.

Here's the tension worth sitting with, and it's the actual reason Lydian is worth knowing. Over a static
chord, Lydian is the more consonant of the two — nothing in it fights the chord the way Ionian's

Start the drone. On the card headed

Be honest about what that actually tests: the drone holds the root, not the full chord, so tapping two chips in a row isn't the clash itself. For that, hold a real
ring over it. Ten seconds, and you'll hear exactly what this lesson has been describing.
"Avoid note" is a bad name for a real thing. Nothing here is forbidden. It's a note to move through, not a note to land on.

Avoid notes turn out to be a general idea, not just an Ionian quirk — a later chapter takes that up properly, once more than one has been met. For now: of this chapter's three modes, only Lydian escapes it.
